articles.title: Maternal sleep latency during early pregnancy is linked to child intelligence scores
articles.summary: Taking a long time to fall asleep during pregnancy is associated with slightly lower offspring intelligence scores at age four. New research points to specific metabolic chemicals in the blood that may link prenatal rest to child brain development.

articles.title: Sex differences in personality traits are shrinking among younger generations
articles.summary: Are men and women becoming more alike? New research analyzing global survey data finds that differences in key economic preferences, such as trust and risk tolerance, are significantly smaller among younger generations than older ones.

articles.title: Temporally constraining source imaging estimates in an underdetermined neural system with eigenmodes of cortical geometry
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.00809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric eigenmodes provide a compact and biologically grounded representation of large-scale neural activity. Previous work demonstrated that they can mitigate the underdetermined nature of electroencephalographic (EEG) and magnetoencephalographic (MEG) source localisation, an ill-posed inverse problem in which neural activity is reconstructed from non-invasive recordings. Beyond their spatial structure, neural field theory predicts the temporal evolution of eigenmodes through analytically derived transfer functions. Motivated by this framework

articles.title: Money problems may age your brain faster
articles.summary: Persistent financial hardship in early and middle adulthood was linked to poorer thinking skills by the 50s and more signs of brain aging later in life. Researchers say years of chronic stress and financial worry may gradually take a toll on the brain.

articles.title: Alzheimer’s may leave a mark on the brain long before plaques appear
articles.summary: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer’s may begin at least seven years before amyloid plaques become detectable with current PET scans. Researchers uncovered the signal by tracking healthy older adults with repeated brain imaging over nearly 20 years. The discovery could help scientists identify Alzheimer’s earlier and suggests that important disease processes may start before visible plaque buildup.

articles.title: Heavy ChatGPT use linked to intellectual laziness and social isolation
articles.summary: New research reveals that relying too heavily on generative artificial intelligence can erode critical thinking, memory, and social skills. However, using the technology thoughtfully as a collaborative tool might actually boost human creativity and confidence.

articles.title: Brain scans shed light on how practice and genetics combine to influence reading ability
articles.summary: Scientists have mapped the reading brain, finding that genetics set the foundation for processing sounds and meaning. Meanwhile, the physical act of reading practice actually thickens specific brain regions and optimizes communication pathways.

articles.title: Brain waves reveal how alcohol cues hijack decision-making in addiction
articles.summary: People with alcohol use disorder experience automatic emotional reactions to alcohol-related images that disrupt their decision-making processes. New research shows the brain attempts to offset these cognitive disruptions by increasing activity in regions associated with deliberate thought.

articles.title: For fibromyalgia, gentle and enjoyable exercise seems to works better than pushing through pain
articles.summary: A new study shows that a tailored, low-intensity exercise program can provide lasting relief for people with fibromyalgia. Brain scans suggest these improvements are linked to metabolic changes in the cerebellum, a region involved in pain processing.

articles.title: Mindfulness may lower blood pressure in just 8 weeks
articles.summary: Mindfulness, gratitude, and optimism training may improve blood pressure, inflammation, and other heart-health measures within just eight to 12 weeks. The strongest programs paired daily practice with regular reinforcement, suggesting that improving psychological well-being could become another tool for protecting cardiovascular health.

articles.title: Scientists find a human-only gene that may help explain our brainpower
articles.summary: Scientists discovered that human microglia, immune cells that help shape developing brain circuits, can take four to eight years to mature instead of just weeks as they do in mice. The unusually slow process may help explain how the human brain develops its remarkable complexity and cognitive abilities.

articles.title: HEPA air purifiers may boost brain function after just one month
articles.summary: Adults aged 40 and older performed about 12% faster on a test of executive function after using a HEPA air purifier at home for one month. The findings suggest that cleaner indoor air could offer a simple way to help protect the brain from the effects of traffic-related pollution.

articles.title: Scientists challenge a 70-year-old “lizard brain” myth
articles.summary: A long-standing picture of brain evolution as newer, rational layers stacked on top of an ancient “lizard brain” may be deeply misleading. Researchers found that evolution instead appears to balance two competing styles of brain wiring, expanding one while shrinking the other depending on what an animal needs to survive.
